Prevention: Skip-row planting patterns and lower in-row plant density improves air movement and ultimately reduces disease impact.
Balanced fertilizer dose also enhances plant vigour and reduces the threat of boll rot.
Irrigation should be applied sufficiently to avoid midseason stress that may induce premature cutout.
Defoliation will also help reduce boll rots.
Thoroughly incorporate crop residues as soon as possible.
Early sowing of crops is a preventive measure for boll rot.
Crop rotation with non-hosts e.g. sowing of sorghum for 3-4 years is useful for control of boll rot.
Monitoring: Rain and high humidity during late summer and fall are optimum conditions for boll-rot development.
Ideal temperatures for boll maturation and opening also favour the growth and spread of boll rot.
Poorly drained soil will retain more water and have higher relative humidity conducive to the spread of the disease.
Insect management must be honed for early detection so as to avoid boll rot.
Vigilant insect scouting and prompt response to confirmed outbreaks diminish injury and subsequent boll rot.
Direct Control: Field drainage should not allow water to back up into the field and inundate low bolls on plants near the tail drain.
